- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot, especially after spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — model is overly conservative, often missing upward reversals.
- Lagged corrections: model often fails to adjust early in bearish sentiment, leading to delayed downside corrections.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating price reversion to historical mean in medium-term horizons.
- Overshoot after spikes: model frequently forecasts a peak after a sharp rise, then underestimates the subsequent decline — especially when sentiment drops sharply.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum, especially when sentiment is high — model ignores structural trends.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.6, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overestimation; if sentiment < 0.3, increase forecast by 5–10% to capture hidden momentum.
